knowledge_point.title: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring and Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we factor the expression:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -{cos}^{3}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡\theta =2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )
$$

Then, we use ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot 1 \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -{cos}^{3}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡\theta =2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .
$$

knowledge_point.title: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring and Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we factor the expression:

$$
{sin}^{3}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {cos}^{2}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ({sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

Then, we use ${sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta =1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ({sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot 1+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that

$$
{sin}^{3}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {cos}^{2}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we factor $\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ from the expression:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x{cos}^{3}⁡x+{sin}^{3}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot ({cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x)
$$

Then, we use ${cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x=1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot ({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot 1 \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x{cos}^{3}⁡x+{sin}^{3}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring and Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we factor ${sin}^{3}⁡x$ from the expression:

$$
{sin}^{5}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x{sin}^{3}⁡x={sin}^{3}⁡x\cdot ({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x)
$$

Then, we use ${sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x=1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{3}⁡x\cdot ({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x) & ={sin}^{3}⁡x\cdot 1 \\  & ={sin}^{3}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that

$$
{sin}^{5}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x{sin}^{3}⁡x={sin}^{3}⁡x.
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we factor ${cos}^{2}⁡x$  from the first two terms:

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡x{cos}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{4}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x={cos}^{2}⁡x\cdot ({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x)+{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

Then, we use ${cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x=1$ to simplify the given expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡x\cdot ({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x)+{sin}^{2}⁡x & ={cos}^{2}⁡x\cdot 1+{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡x{cos}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{4}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x=1.
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we factor the expression:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2{cos}^{3}⁡x+2{sin}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2\operatorname{cos}⁡x({cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x)
$$

Then, we use ${cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x=1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2\operatorname{cos}⁡x({cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot 1 \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2{cos}^{3}⁡x+2{sin}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring and Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we factor the expression:

$$
-2\sin^{5}{\alpha}-2\sin^{3}{\alpha}\cos^{2}{\alpha}-3\sin^{2}{\alpha}\cos^{3}{\alpha}-3\cos^{5}{\alpha}=-2\sin^{3}{\alpha}\cdot(\sin^{2}{\alpha}+\cos^{2}{\alpha})-3\cos^{3}{\alpha}\cdot(\sin^{2}{\alpha}+\cos^{2}{\alpha})
$$

Then, we use $\sin^{2}{\alpha}+\cos^{2}{\alpha}=1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2\sin^{3}{\alpha}\cdot(\sin^{2}{\alpha}+\cos^{2}{\alpha})-3\cos^{3}{\alpha}\cdot(\sin^{2}{\alpha}+\cos^{2}{\alpha}) & =-2\sin^{3}{\alpha}\cdot 1-3\cos^{3}{\alpha}\cdot 1 \\  & =-2\sin^{3}{\alpha}-3\cos^{3}{\alpha}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that

$$
-2\sin^{5}{\alpha}-2\sin^{3}{\alpha}\cos^{2}{\alpha}-3\sin^{2}{\alpha}\cos^{3}{\alpha}-3\cos^{5}{\alpha}=-2\sin^{3}{\alpha}-3\cos^{3}{\alpha}.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring and Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we factor the expression:

$$
-4\sin^{4}{t}\cos{t}-4\sin^{2}{t}\cos^{3}{t}=-4\sin^{2}{t}\cos{t}\cdot(\sin^{2}{t}+\cos^{2}{t})
$$

Then, we use $\sin^{2}{t}+\cos^{2}{t}=1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4\sin^{2}{t}\cos{t}\cdot(\sin^{2}{t}+\cos^{2}{t}) & =-4\sin^{2}{t}\cos{t}\cdot 1 \\  & =-4\sin^{2}{t}\cos{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that

$$
-4\sin^{4}{t}\cos{t}-4\sin^{2}{t}\cos^{3}{t}=-4\sin^{2}{t}\cos{t}.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring and Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we factor the expression:

$$
-2\sin^{3}{t}-2\sin{t}\cos^{2}{t}-4\sin^{2}{t}\cos{t}-4\cos^{3}{t}=-2\sin{t}\cdot(\sin^{2}{t}+\cos^{2}{t})-4\cos{t}\cdot(\sin^{2}{t}+\cos^{2}{t})
$$

Then, we use $\sin^{2}{t}+\cos^{2}{t}=1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2\sin{t}\cdot(\sin^{2}{t}+\cos^{2}{t})-4\cos{t}\cdot(\sin^{2}{t}+\cos^{2}{t}) & =-2\sin{t}\cdot 1-4\cos{t}\cdot 1 \\  & =-2\sin{t}-4\cos{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that

$$
-2\sin^{3}{t}-2\sin{t}\cos^{2}{t}-4\sin^{2}{t}\cos{t}-4\cos^{3}{t}=-2\sin{t}-4\cos{t}.
$$

First, we factor the expression:

$$
4\sin^{5}{\theta}+4\sin^{3}{\theta}\cos^{2}{\theta}-4\sin^{2}{\theta}\cos^{3}{\theta}-4\cos^{5}{\theta}=4\sin^{3}{\theta}\cdot(\sin^{2}{\theta}+\cos^{2}{\theta})-4\cos^{3}{\theta}\cdot(\sin^{2}{\theta}+\cos^{2}{\theta})
$$

Then, we use $\sin^{2}{\theta}+\cos^{2}{\theta}=1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}4\sin^{3}{\theta}\cdot(\sin^{2}{\theta}+\cos^{2}{\theta})-4\cos^{3}{\theta}\cdot(\sin^{2}{\theta}+\cos^{2}{\theta}) & =4\sin^{3}{\theta}\cdot 1-4\cos^{3}{\theta}\cdot 1 \\  & =4\sin^{3}{\theta}-4\cos^{3}{\theta}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that

$$
4\sin^{5}{\theta}+4\sin^{3}{\theta}\cos^{2}{\theta}-4\sin^{2}{\theta}\cos^{3}{\theta}-4\cos^{5}{\theta}=4\sin^{3}{\theta}-4\cos^{3}{\theta}.
$$

$$
-5\sin^{4}{\alpha}-5\sin^{2}{\alpha}\cos^{2}{\alpha}=-5\sin^{2}{\alpha}\cdot(\sin^{2}{\alpha}+\cos^{2}{\alpha})
$$

Then, we use $\sin^{2}{\alpha}+\cos^{2}{\alpha}=1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$

$$

$$

knowledge_point.title: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring and Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we factor the expression:

$$
-2\sin^{3}{\alpha}-2\sin{\alpha}\cos^{2}{\alpha}+3\sin{\alpha}=-2\sin{\alpha}\cdot(\sin^{2}{\alpha}+\cos^{2}{\alpha})+3\sin{\alpha}
$$

Then, we use $\sin^{2}{\alpha}+\cos^{2}{\alpha}=1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2\sin{\alpha}\cdot(\sin^{2}{\alpha}+\cos^{2}{\alpha})+3\sin{\alpha} & =-2\sin{\alpha}\cdot 1+3\sin{\alpha} \\  & =-2\sin{\alpha}+3\sin{\alpha} \\  & =\sin{\alpha}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that

$$
-2\sin^{3}{\alpha}-2\sin{\alpha}\cos^{2}{\alpha}+3\sin{\alpha}=\sin{\alpha}.
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we factor the expression:

$$
-3\sin^{5}{t}-3\sin^{3}{t}\cos^{2}{t}+4\sin^{2}{t}\cos{t}+4\cos^{3}{t}=-3\sin^{3}{t}\cdot(\sin^{2}{t}+\cos^{2}{t})+4\cos{t}\cdot(\sin^{2}{t}+\cos^{2}{t})
$$

Then, we use $\sin^{2}{t}+\cos^{2}{t}=1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3\sin^{3}{t}\cdot(\sin^{2}{t}+\cos^{2}{t})+4\cos{t}\cdot(\sin^{2}{t}+\cos^{2}{t}) & =-3\sin^{3}{t}\cdot 1+4\cos{t}\cdot 1 \\  & =-3\sin^{3}{t}+4\cos{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that

$$
-3\sin^{5}{t}-3\sin^{3}{t}\cos^{2}{t}+4\sin^{2}{t}\cos{t}+4\cos^{3}{t}=-3\sin^{3}{t}+4\cos{t}.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring and Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we factor the expression:

$$
4\sin^{3}{x}\cos^{2}{x}+4\sin{x}\cos^{4}{x}=4\sin{x}\cos^{2}{x}\cdot(\sin^{2}{x}+\cos^{2}{x})
$$

Then, we use $\sin^{2}{x}+\cos^{2}{x}=1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}4\sin{x}\cos^{2}{x}\cdot(\sin^{2}{x}+\cos^{2}{x}) & =4\sin{x}\cos^{2}{x}\cdot 1 \\  & =4\sin{x}\cos^{2}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that

$$
4\sin^{3}{x}\cos^{2}{x}+4\sin{x}\cos^{4}{x}=4\sin{x}\cos^{2}{x}.
$$

$$
-3\sin^{5}{t}-3\sin^{3}{t}\cos^{2}{t}-\sin^{2}{t}\cos^{3}{t}-\cos^{5}{t}=-3\sin^{3}{t}\cdot(\sin^{2}{t}+\cos^{2}{t})-\cos^{3}{t}\cdot(\sin^{2}{t}+\cos^{2}{t})

$$
\begin{aligned}-3\sin^{3}{t}\cdot(\sin^{2}{t}+\cos^{2}{t})-\cos^{3}{t}\cdot(\sin^{2}{t}+\cos^{2}{t}) & =-3\sin^{3}{t}\cdot 1-\cos^{3}{t}\cdot 1 \\  & =-3\sin^{3}{t}-\cos^{3}{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that

$$
-3\sin^{5}{t}-3\sin^{3}{t}\cos^{2}{t}-\sin^{2}{t}\cos^{3}{t}-\cos^{5}{t}=-3\sin^{3}{t}-\cos^{3}{t}.
$$
